1: Chapter 1: The Visitor on a Rainy Night

The rain over Qingshi Town had been falling for three full days. Lin Xiaoyu's older sister had left for the capital in the spring, and ever since then, she had been the only one looking after the little pharmacy in town.
After dark, she shut the doors and windows, counted the day's earnings, blew out the oil lamp, and went upstairs.
She had just lain down when urgent knocking came from downstairs, followed by a man's voice: "Is anyone there?"
Outside stood a young man soaked to the skin, his left arm wrapped in a blood-soaked strip of cloth. He said his name was Bai Yun, and that he was from the Azure Dragon Society.
"I need my wound bandaged," Bai Yun said in a low voice. "I can pay. Will three thousand five hundred wen be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oil paper from inside his robe. "This letter must be delivered to Qingfeng Temple before the eighteenth of the fifth month."
While she bandaged him, he gave a wry smile and said, "If my fiancée knew I was knocking on a girl's door in the middle of the night, she'd definitely be jealous."
Lin Xiaoyu didn't take his money. She only said, "Tomorrow morning, I'll take you up the mountain."
2: They set out at first light. Lin Xiaoyu carried a bamboo basket on her back, packed with dry rations, herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the mountain, they ran into old Zhou Dashan, who was gathering firewood. The old man set down his axe and lowered his voice, saying that at dusk the previous day, three strangers had been at the town entrance asking about a wounded young man.
"Xiaoyu, take the small path," Zhou Dashan said. "The main road isn't safe." Lin Xiaoyu thanked him.
The narrow path was slippery. Lin Xiaoyu walked ahead, placing each step with care. Bai Yun followed behind without a word.

By noon the rain had stopped. The mist among the mountains slowly thinned, and in the distance the roof of Qingfeng Temple came into view. A nun stood at the temple gate—Zhao Qiuyue, the temple's guest keeper, responsible for receiving visitors.
Zhao Qiuyue took the letter, examined the red seal on the flap, and nodded. "The abbot has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Bai Yun said to Lin Xiaoyu, "I owe you my life." Lin Xiaoyu smiled. "Then next time you come, help me fix the roof of my medicine shop." Bai Yun stayed at the temple.
At dusk, Lin Xiaoyu made her way down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home it was already dark. She lit a lamp and sat behind the counter for a long while.
